assistance: AI-assisted (Claude): the TypeScript generator generators/nyc-ellis-island.ts was written from the open evidence in the modelling notes (OSM, public lidar and aerials, licensed photographs, published dimensions), reviewed by a human against reference photos, and exported deterministically. modelingNotes: Ellis Island Main Building (National Museum of Immigration) — procedural, CC0-1.0, no textures. bun generators/nyc-ellis-island.ts

Map frame: x = model east, y = model north, z up, metres. The front, with the three great arches and the entrance canopy, faces model south (true bearing ~225°, towards the ferry slip). Placed at bearing 44.5°, the outline's long walls. Anchor: area centroid of the OSM outline way/95161971.

OSM way/95161971 (outline, 118 × 66 m: the wings, the front recessed between the towers, the rear annex; 3 levels, roof #946e48) and its parts 1177355003/004 (two glass hipped skylights on the west wing).

Lidar: USGS 3DEP NY_NewYorkCity (2017), in the model frame (/tmp/city/nyc/work/nyc-ellis-island/bands.png), above the lowest ground (1.6 m NAVD88): the wings' flat roofs 18.2 m, parapets 19.5 m; the front and rear blocks between the towers 19.7 m; the Great Hall's clerestory x -30…30, y -15…5.5, walls to ~26 m under a red gabled roof, ridge 29 m along x, its gable ends at x = ±30; the four towers, 8 × 8 m, at x ±(19…28), y -29…-21 and 12…20, domes to ~35 m and finials to 38.5–41 m; the rear annex 7.5 m; the canopy 17 m wide, 32 m long (y -25…-57), eaves ~5 m, ridge ~7.6 m.
NAIP orthophoto (USGS, public domain): the hall's red tile roof, the wings' dark flat roofs and skylights, the canopy's glazed roof.

Published: 1900, Boring & Tilton, French Renaissance Revival; red brick in Flemish bond with limestone trim; four towers with copper domes; the Great Hall (Registry Room) on the second floor behind three great arched windows; the red steel and glass entrance canopy reproduces the original's form (Wikipedia; NRHP 66000119; NPS).

Photos, credits in /tmp/city/nyc/work/nyc-ellis-island/photos/credits.txt: the front and canopy (chensiyuan, CC BY-SA 4.0), from the south-west and west over the water (Jakub Hałun, CC BY 4.0), an aerial from the south (public domain), others by Simeon87, Dmckelvey4, Bohao Zhao.

Estimated: storey heights and window counts (from the front photo scaled to the lidar's 19.7 m cornice), the tower stages (limestone to the cornice, the banded brick shaft to 29 m, the lantern to 31.6 m, the onion dome to 35.8 m, the spire to 40.6 m within the lidar's 38.5–41 m), the front gables (apex 23.5 m), the canopy's posts and roof, the rear and wing-end windows (drawn like the front). The skylights on the wings are left as flat roof.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "nyc-ellis-island", model "nyc-ellis-island"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/c3921f733df14b41e1f6d15853cce7b343886f17/generators/nyc-ellis-island.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
